question.text: SEBI decides to conduct an inspection of the books and records of 'Narmada Credit Opportunities Fund' under SEBI (AIF) Regulations. What is the standard notice SEBI must give, and can inspection be conducted without notice?

answer.text: 30 days' notice is mandatory; no-notice inspection is not permitted under any circumstances
No notice is required for any inspection
60 days' notice is standard; inspection without notice requires a court order
10-day notice is standard; however, in the interest of investors, SEBI may by written order direct inspection without notice

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook explains that SEBI shall give 10 days' notice before ordering an inspection of an AIF's books and records. The same provision allows SEBI, in the interest of investors and by a written order, to direct that an inspection be carried out without giving such notice. This combination is what the keyed option captures. The Trap: Option A overstates the notice period at 30 days and wrongly says no-notice inspection is never permitted, ignoring the investor-interest override. Option B drops the notice requirement entirely. Option C invents a 60-day period and a court-order condition that the workbook does not impose for the no-notice carve-out. Note: Lock in two elements: a default 10-day notice for inspection, and a written-order carve-out allowing SEBI to inspect without notice when it considers it necessary in the interest of investors.
